text:
anna: Heads-up — seeing a ~18% p99 latency regression on Mistral-8B after yesterday's kernel selector change. Only for chat workloads with system prompts. CPU/GPU util looks normal.

mike: yep noticed that on the dashboards. Only on the hosted tier and Dedicated with batch size >1.

jin: can we reproduce locally? any difference by model (llama/mixtral/qwen)?

anna: repro is pretty consistent on Mistral and Mixtral variants. Qwen seems less affected. Llama shows a tiny bump.

lisa: quick hypothesis: the new kernel selector prefers the byte-fallback tokenization path for some special tokens used in our chat templates, which ends up changing token counts and breaking our KV cache warmup assumptions.

mike: that matches an observation — traces show more short-lived KV allocations and lower cache hit ratio. p99 spikes exactly when the first streamed response starts.

perf-bot: perf trace attached: /perf/traces/1776001234/trace-1.pb (note: this is a simulated path in thread)

jin: can you paste the config we shipped?

anna: shipped selector config:```json
{"policy":"cost-first","fallback":"byte_fallback_if_unknown","min_batch_tokens":8,"dynamic_window_ms":25}
```

sam: the byte_fallback_if_unknown was intended for robust tokenization, but on Mistral it triggers for sequences with emojis + rare unicode and returns 2-3x tokens for same string. That explodes effective sequence length.

lisa: also RoPE scaling: Mistral's RoPE implementation with head_dim mismatch seems to increase matrix size slightly when we pick the alternate kernel. The kernel's kernel-selection heuristics don't account for head_count * kv_dim alignment, so we get suboptimal matmul paths.

mike: tl;dr: tokenizer -> more tokens -> batching window picks larger tokens-per-request -> KV cache warmed for wrong key shapes -> fallback kernel does extra copies.

anna: I ran a small A/B on dedicated pool: revert selector to prefer architecture-optimized kernels (prefer 'arch_kern_v2' for Mistral) and force tokenizer strict mode (no byte fallback). p99 dropped back to baseline within 1 hour.

jin: important to record which models/configs changed:
- Mistral-8B: arch_kern_v2 preferred -> good
- Mixtral-7B: similar but needs head_dim patch (apply kv-align patch)
- Qwen-7B: unaffected (different tokenizer path)

sam: action items:
- anna: collect tokenization diffs for a sample of system prompts (10k requests) and save token histograms
- mike: roll kernel selector config to canary and add metric for "kv_cache_hit_ratio"
- jin: run microbench of matmul kernels with head_count x kv_dim combos we use
- lisa: check chat template prefixes for hidden special chars (BOMs, zero-width joiners)

anna: here's a quick command I used to collect token diffs:```bash
python -m tools.token_diff --model mistral-8b --input-corpus system_prompts.jsonl --mode strict > /tmp/tokdiff.csv
```

mike: for profiling, use nvprof/cupti and also our pprof agent. Example perf flags: `--trace-kv --trace-kernel --trace-tokenizer` (the traces are large).

lisa: note on RoPE: we saw tiny differences when RoPE roots were scaled to 1.02 for long contexts; that caused slightly different attention perf due to changed transpose ordering in the fused kernel. If selector flips to unfused kernel we pay penalty.

jin: on the batcher heuristics side: current policy groups by model+route and uses token_count estimate from tokenizer. If tokenizer estimation changes due to byte fallback we get large variability inside a batch leading to tail latency. We should consider capping per-request token estimate contribution when unknown tokens present.

sam: suggestion: add a small penalty to routes that require byte_fallback so the batcher prefers routes with stable tokenization. That should reduce mixed-batch variance.

anna: experiment plan:
1) revert selector for Mistral on canary (done)
2) disable byte_fallback in tokenizer for canary only (done)
3) run 24h token histogram and batch composition report
4) run kernel microbench for head/kv combos we use and update selector scoring function to include head_dim alignment cost

mike: I'm adding new telemetry metric: `kernel_selector_reason` with tags {model, kernel_chosen, head_kv_align, tokenizer_mode}. Will surface in console.

lisa: small gotcha — some partners rely on byte fallback for weird encodings; if we change defaults we need a config flag for tenant-level override. Add that to the canary notes.

anna: agreed. For now canary will be "strict_tokenizer_by_default" but tenant override remains. We'll notify partner teams.

jin: after we get perf numbers, we should run quality checks (few eval prompts) to ensure disabling byte fallback didn't change model outputs in important ways. Might affect parsing of weird characters in prompts.

sam: ops checklist for rollback if things go sideways:
- revert selector config (1 click)
- enable tenant byte_fallback global flag
- re-warm KV caches (we have a warmup job)

anna: I pushed a small PR with the selector scoring changes and tests: https://git.redwood/infra/selectors/pull/412 (placeholder link).

mike: I'll watch canary dashboards. If we get stable numbers, let's bake head/kv align into selector and make tokenizer change opt-in per-tenant.

lisa: noted — I'll scan chat templates for hidden chars and sanitize server-side for the canary.

anna: thanks everyone. I'll post the token histograms when ready and attach perf traces. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: summary note saved to /reports/1776001234/summary.txt

mike: thanks — great triage.

anna: closing the loop later today with numbers.
